questions.question: When a number is increased by 216, it becomes 140% of itself. What is the number?
questions.solution:
'Becomes 140% of itself' means the increase is 
the extra 40%. 
 Step 1   Write it. 
x + 216 = 1.4x 
 Step 2   Solve. 
0.4x = 216   ∴  x = 540

questions.question: Two numbers are 40% and 80% less than a third number. By how much percent is the second number to be enhanced to make it equal to the first number?
questions.solution:
Both are measured off the third number, so give 
it 100. 
 Step 1   Fix all three. 
C = 100   ⇒  A = 60,   B = 20 
 Step 2   Lift B to A, measured on B. 
(60 − 20)/20 × 100 = 200%

questions.question: Price of diesel increased from Rs. 45/litre to Rs. 50/litre. How much should the consumption of diesel be reduced (in %) so as to increase expenditure by only 5% ?
questions.solution:
Expenditure = price × quantity. Fix the old 
product, then divide by the NEW price. 
 Step 1   Old expenditure, with quantity 100. 
45 × 100 = ₹4,500 
 Step 2   It may rise by 5%. 
4,500 × 1.05 = ₹4,725 
 Step 3   What that buys at ₹50. 
4,725 / 50 = 94.5   ⇒  cut = 5.5%

questions.question: Price of a ticket of a show of circus is Rs. 12. When the price of the ticket is reduced then the audience is increased by 80% and the total income is increased by 20%. Find the price of the ticket after reduction.
questions.solution:
Work in total collection: audience × ticket price. 
 Step 1   Take the audience as 100. 
old income = 12 × 100 = 1,200 
 Step 2   Audience +80%, income +20%. 
audience = 180,   income = 1,440 
 Step 3   New ticket price. 
1,440 / 180 = ₹8

questions.question: The length and breadth of the room are decreased by y%. If the cost of painting the room goes down by 30.27%, what is the value of y?
questions.solution:
Two dimensions each cut by y% — the cross term 
matters. 
 Step 1   Area change. 
−2y + y²/100 = −30.27 
 Step 2   Test the options rather than solving the 
quadratic. 
y = 16 → 30.44 ✗        y = 16.5 → 33 − 2.7225 = 
30.2775 ✓

questions.question: A student scores 38% and fails by 12 marks. If passing is 40%, what are the maximum marks of the exam? Volume factor 1000 x 1.1 (l +10%) 1100 x 1.1
questions.solution:
The marks he falls short by ARE the percentage 
gap — that is the whole question. 
 Step 1   The gap. 
40% − 38% = 2%,  which is the 12 marks 
 Step 2   So one percent, then the total. 
1% = 6   ∴  maximum marks = 600

questions.question: 62 ½ % of a number exceeds 25% of the same number by 15. What is the number?
questions.solution:
Step 1   As fractions. 
62½% = 5/8        25% = 2/8 
 Step 2   Their difference is the 15. 
(3/8)x = 15   ∴  x = 40

questions.question: A square plot of land is to be expanded such that its area becomes 225% of the original. By what percentage must each side be increased?
questions.solution:
Area scales as the SQUARE of the side — so take 
the square root. 
 Step 1   Area factor. 
225% = 2.25 
 Step 2   Side factor. 
√2.25 = 1.5   ⇒  each side up 50%

 Step 1   Radius factor. 
4.9 / 3.5 = 7/5 
 Step 2   Cube it. 
(7/5)³ = 343/125   ⇒  rise = 218/125 × 100 = 174.4%

questions.question: Aditya buys 300 mangoes for Rs. 1100. Some of these mangoes are rotten and thrown away. He sells the remaining mangoes at Rs. 5 each and makes a profit of Rs. 150. Find the percentage of mangoes thrown away.
questions.solution:
Step 1   Money taken. 
1,100 + 150 = ₹1,250   ⇒  1,250 / 5 = 250 mangoes 
sold 
 Step 2   So thrown away. 
300 − 250 = 50   ⇒  50/300 × 100 = 16⅔%

87.5% of 400 = 350        92% of 250 = 230 
 Step 3   So the women. 
350 − 230 = 120   ⇒  120/150 = 80%

questions.question: X is 35% less than Y, Z is 40% more than the sum of X and Y. By what percent is Z more than two times X
questions.solution:
Step 1   X and Z. 
X = 65        Z = 1.4(65 + 100) = 231

(231 − 130)/130 × 100 = 77.7%

questions.question: Due to 20% reduction in the price of wheat per kg, Ram is able to buy 5 kg more for Rs. 800. What is the original quantity (in kg) of wheat?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Quantity ratio. 
old : new = 4 : 5 
 Step 2   The extra 5 kg is one part. 
1 part = 5 kg   ∴  original = 4 parts = 20 kg

questions.question: 24% of Reena's Salary is equal to 38% of Sunita's Salary. Veena's salary is two-third of the total salary of Reena and Sunita. If Veena's Salary is Rs. 62,000 then Sunita's Salary is.
questions.solution:
Cross-multiply the two salary percentages to fix 
their ratio first. 
 Step 1   Reena against Sunita. 
24R = 38S   ⇒  R : S = 38 : 24 = 19 : 12 
 Step 2   Veena is two-thirds of the pair. 
(2/3)(19 + 12)k = 62k/3 = 62,000   ⇒  k = 3,000 
 Step 3   Sunita. 
12 × 3,000 = ₹36,000

questions.question: A shopkeeper has a certain number of apples of which 10% are found to be rotten. He sells 85% of the remaining good apples and still has 405 good apples. How many apples did he originally have?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Take 100 apples. 
10% rotten  ⇒  90 good 
 Step 2   He sells 85% of those. 
left = 15% of 90 = 13.5 
 Step 3   That 13.5 stands for 405. 
100 × 405/13.5 = 3,000 apples

questions.solution:
Step 1   Write both. 
M + F = 18,000        0.05M + 0.07F = 1,200 
 Step 2   Substitute and solve. 
900 + 0.02F = 1,200   ⇒  F = 15,000,  M = 3,000

questions.question: Entry ticket of a cinema hall is Rs. 250. When the price is reduced by a certain percentage then the sales of ticket increase by 50%, whereas the overall collection is reduced by 17.5%. Find the percentage decrease in the price of the ticket.
questions.solution:
Collection = price × tickets 
 Step 1   Let the new price be x, sales 1.5 times. 
1.5x = 0.825 × 250 
 Step 2   Solve. 
x = 206.25 / 1.5 = ₹137.50 
 Step 3   The fall. 
(250 − 137.5)/250 × 100 = 45%

questions.question: When the price of sugar increased by 28%, a family reduced its consumption per month such that the expenditure on sugar was only 12% more than the earlier one. If the family consumed 18.4 kg sugar per month earlier, then what is its new consumption of sugar per month?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Quantity factor. 
112/128 = 7/8 
 Step 2   Apply it to 18.4 kg. 
18.4 × 7/8 = 16.1 kg

income 100,  expenditure 80,  savings 20

income 125,  expenditure 104   ⇒  savings 21

5% of ₹7,120 = ₹356

questions.question: Suresh can save 20% of his income. But after 4 years, his income increases by 40% and he still manages to save the same amount as before. What is the percent increase in his expenditure ?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Before. 
income 100,  savings 20,  expenditure 80 
 Step 2   After a 40% rise, savings unchanged. 
income 140,  savings 20   ⇒  expenditure 120 
 Step 3   Rise in expenditure. 
40/80 × 100 = 50%

questions.question: In a city 39% of the men are married and 51% of the women are married. Considering that nobody is married more than once. What percent of the population is married?
questions.solution:
Married men and married women are the SAME 
couples counted twice. 
 Step 1   Equate the two counts. 
39% of M = 51% of W   ⇒  M : W = 51 : 39 = 17 : 13 
 Step 2   Take M = 17 × 100 and W = 13 × 100. 
married = 39(17) + 51(13) = 663 + 663 = 1,326  out 
of 3,000 
 Step 3   As a percentage. 
1,326 / 3,000 × 100 = 44.2%

questions.solution:

15 + 40 + 10 + 15 = 80% 
 Step 2   So the EMI. 
20% of 80,000 = ₹16,000

questions.question: A metallic conical bowl with base radius 10 cm and height 24 cm is uniformly heated, increasing all dimensions by 10%. By how much does the volume increase?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Every dimension up 10%. 
volume factor = (11/10)³ = 1,331/1,000 
 Step 2   The rise. 
331/1,000 = 33.1%

questions.question: A student needs at least 60% to pass. He got 40% on the first exam, 70% on the second and x% on the third (equal weightage). What is the minimum x% to pass?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Three papers at 60% each. 
needed = 3 × 60 = 180 points 
 Step 2   He already has. 
40 + 70 = 110   ∴  x = 70

4x − x = 75   ⇒  x = 25,  y = 100
